metaDescription: Six cordless handheld and compact vacuums for trade, jobsite and office use, compared on filtration, tank size, battery platform and wet or dry pickup.
expertTake: The DeWalt 20V HEPA handheld is the best pick for tradespeople who sweep drywall and concrete dust off tools and benches every day. The Milwaukee M18 compact wet/dry units are the value pick if you already own M18 batteries. Anyone cleaning large floors for a living should skip handhelds entirely and buy a backpack or commercial upright.
introParagraphs: No major maker sells a true industrial handheld vacuum in the way it sells a drill. What exists is a small set of cordless units that tradespeople, janitorial crews and workshop owners adopt because they share batteries with the tools already on the truck. They differ from household dustbusters in filtration, capacity and abuse tolerance.

That changes how you shop. Dust type, wet or dry pickup, tank size and battery platform matter more than a pretty design, and many listings are bare tools sold without a pack or charger. The six picks here cover the real choices in light commercial use.

products.name: DeWalt 20V handheld vacuum with HEPA filter and 6 attachments
products.description:
This is the commercial pick because its filter is built for fine construction dust. A HEPA filter captures the particle sizes that drywall sanding and concrete cutting throw off, which a plain foam filter lets straight through into the air you breathe. For crews working in finished rooms, that difference is the whole reason to buy a dedicated tool.

It runs on the DeWalt 20V battery family, so one pack on the truck serves both drill and vacuum, and the listing quotes a long run with a large pack. Six attachments and an LED light cover benches, vehicle interiors and ceiling corners. It is dry only, so unlike the DeWalt hand vac below it cannot take a spill, and it is a handheld first, not a tank on wheels.

Push-button canister release makes emptying fast between jobs. Rinse or replace the HEPA element on a schedule that matches your dust load, since drywall dust clogs it quickly and a clogged filter chokes airflow. Keep the battery off the truck dashboard in summer, and check the listing to confirm whether a battery and charger come in the box. A simple habit helps with fine dust: tap the canister out outdoors or into a bag held close to the opening, so the cloud you were trying to remove does not drift back into the room. Pair it with a quick wipe of the HEPA seat each time, because a bit of caked dust under the gasket lets air leak around the filter and defeats the point of paying for it.
products.bestFor: Tradespeople dealing with drywall, plaster and concrete dust.
pros: Six attachments cover benches and cabs
cons: Fine dust clogs the HEPA element fast

products.name: DeWalt 20V MAX wet or dry hand vacuum, 1/2-gallon tank
products.description:
The distinctive thing here is the wet/dry rating. A rated filter and tank mean you can pick up a spill of coolant or a puddle at a sink without the usual fear of ruining a dry-only motor. The filter is described as a HEPA-class wet/dry type, and it can be washed and reused.

A front utility nozzle handles floors and benches, while an extendable rubber hose reaches into engine bays and ductwork. The half-gallon tank is larger than a typical home dustbuster bowl and smaller than the Milwaukee tanks, so it sits mid-pack in capacity. It is sold bare tool, meaning battery and charger are extra unless a kit is listed.

After wet use, empty the tank and dry the filter fully before storing, because a damp filter in a closed tank grows mould in a week. Check the latch seals for sand, and rinse the tank with a hose. A wet pickup of oily fluid needs a proper wash or the smell lingers. In a shop where you clear metal swarf, steer clear of the filter edge, since sharp chips cut the pleats and let dust straight through. Replace the filter at the first sign of tearing instead of patching it, because a damaged element is invisible in use and shows up only as dust on the exhaust side.
products.bestFor: Mechanics and installers who need wet and dry pickup on the 20V platform.
pros: Rated for wet or dry cleanup
cons: Bare tool, battery and charger extra

products.name: Milwaukee M18 VC2-0 compact wet/dry vacuum, tool only
products.description:
This is Milwaukee's compact cordless wet/dry vacuum, and it leans toward the portable end of the shop-vac category rather than a pistol-grip handheld. The 7.5 liter tank is a quarter bigger than the DeWalt half-gallon tank, and the unit is carried by handle, not held in one hand like a dustbuster.

It shares the M18 battery family, so crews already on that system get a vacuum without buying a second charger ecosystem. The listing quotes a quiet 69 decibels, which is useful in occupied offices and shops, although noise figures on listings are not independently verified. Compared with the larger FPOVCL, it is the lighter and cheaper choice for small jobs.

Empty the tank after wet work and let it dry with the lid off. Wash the filter when airflow drops, and check the hose for splits where it flexes at the inlet. As a tool-only listing, it needs a battery you already own. In a service call it rides well beside a toolbox: you can clear a work area before you leave and the tank rinses clean afterwards. The compact size also means a single large battery can run through several short clean-ups before it needs a recharge, though the listing gives no runtime figure you should rely on.
products.bestFor: M18 owners who want a quiet, portable wet/dry unit for small jobs.
pros: Listed noise is low for the class
cons: Carried by handle, not truly handheld

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FPOVCL 2.5-gallon cordless wet/dry vacuum
products.description:
At 2.5 gallons this is the largest tank in the lineup, and it is closer to a small shop vacuum than a handheld. A listed 47 inch water lift is a pressure figure, and it hints at real lifting power for wet debris, although a listed wattage of 800 W is a motor rating, not a measure of cleaning ability.

It is the machine for a crew that clears debris from a whole jobsite room each day and wants one tank to hold it all. The listing also quotes 87 decibels, so it is far louder than the quiet VC2-0, and you would not want it running next to a client in an office. Choose it over the compact unit only when tank size, not carry weight, is your limit.

Wet pickup demands a drained and rinsed tank at day's end. Wipe the filter cage, check the float if one is fitted, and keep the hose free of kinks. A full 2.5 gallon tank of wet debris is heavy, so empty at half full. Plan on a proper battery, not the smallest pack in the toolbox, since a larger motor drains a small pack quickly. If hearing protection is already part of your site routine, the noise listing matters less, but a shared workspace deserves the quieter unit.
products.bestFor: Crews that need the largest cordless tank in the lineup.

products.name: Black+Decker dustbuster AdvancedClean with rotating nozzle
products.description:
Not every commercial space needs a jobsite tool. For a reception desk, a break room or a salon station, a classic pistol-grip dustbuster is quicker to grab than a tank on a strap and lighter in the hand. The rotating nozzle follows tabletops and chair seats without twisting your wrist.

It lacks the filtration and tank volume of the DeWalt and Milwaukee units, and a commercial buyer should treat it as a crumb catcher, not a dust control tool. Placed next to the HEPA DeWalt, the gap shows in how fine dust passes through a basic filter. As a low-cost second vacuum for the front-of-house, it is hard to fault.

Tap out the bowl daily and wash the filter if the manual allows. Mount the charging base on a wall so it is always ready, and replace the unit when runtime shrinks, since sealed packs are not designed to be swapped. Keep a second one in a different room if the space is large, because walking a cordless unit across a building to charge it defeats the convenience. Used this way, it earns its place by being the one tool nobody hesitates to pick up.
products.bestFor: Offices, salons and reception desks needing a light daily crumb catcher.
pros: Fast to grab and light in the hand
Rotating nozzle suits desks and seats

products.name: Black+Decker dustbuster Reveal with LED light and charging base
products.description:
Reveal fits a different corner of commercial work: vehicles, storerooms and delivery vans where dim corners hide crumbs. The headlight shows debris under seats and shelves, and a charging base with an indicator tells you whether the pack is ready before a shift.

It is a consumer-grade design, so it is the lightest-duty pick in this group and has no HEPA element or wet rating. In a company van where drivers eat lunch, it does the job better than a jobsite vacuum that nobody wants to carry in.

Wipe the lens, empty the bowl and keep the charging contacts clean. Because it sits in vehicles, watch for heat, since a parked van can cook a lithium pack in an afternoon.
products.bestFor: Delivery vans and company cars where visibility matters.
cons: Heat in a parked van shortens battery life

buyingCriteria.criterion: Filtration for the dust you make
buyingCriteria.explanation: Drywall, concrete and wood dust include very fine particles. The DeWalt HEPA handheld is the only unit in this lineup built around a HEPA element for dry dust, while the wet/dry DeWalt uses a washable HEPA-class filter. Basic foam filters, such as the dustbuster's, let fine dust through and are no substitute.

A dry-only unit like the DeWalt HEPA handheld can be ruined by a liquid pickup. The DeWalt hand vac, the M18 VC2-0 and the FPOVCL are the wet/dry options here. Check the rating before sucking up a spill, because wet use in a dry filter ruins both.

A 1/2-gallon tank suits bench and vehicle work, the VC2-0's 7.5 liters suits a room, and the FPOVCL's 2.5 gallons suits a jobsite zone. Bigger tanks hold more but weigh more when full. Pick the smallest that avoids stopping to empty mid-job.

Buying into the platform you already own saves money, since a battery and charger are the costly part. DeWalt 20V and Milwaukee M18 units share packs with the rest of the truck. Many listings are bare tools, so confirm what is in the box.
Listings quote 69 dB for the VC2-0 and 87 dB for the FPOVCL, a large gap. A loud vacuum is a problem in offices and clinics. Take noise listings as a guide, not a lab figure.

Tool-platform units are built to be dropped and rinsed more than household dustbusters. Replaceable filters and latch seals matter in year three. A consumer dustbuster is cheaper to replace but not designed for site abuse.

specDecoder.meaning: A HEPA filter captures very fine particles at a rated efficiency. It only helps if the housing seals around it.
specDecoder.watchFor: Handhelds seldom use a fully sealed system, so treat HEPA as better, not perfect.

specDecoder.meaning: Measured in inches, it is the pressure the vacuum can pull and indicates lifting power for wet debris. It is not airflow.
specDecoder.watchFor: The FPOVCL's 47 inches is listed alongside a 800 W figure that is a motor rating.

specDecoder.meaning: Measured in gallons or liters, it sets how often you empty and how heavy the vacuum gets when full.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 7.5 liter VC2-0 and 2.5 gallon FPOVCL differ in carry weight more than in features.

specDecoder.meaning: Noise is perceived on a log scale, so a gap of 18 dB is large. Listings rarely state test conditions.
specDecoder.watchFor: 69 dB for the VC2-0 against 87 dB for the FPOVCL is a real difference.

specDecoder.meaning: A bare tool ships without battery or charger. It is cheaper only if you already own a compatible pack.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DeWalt hand vac and the VC2-0 are bare-tool listings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated filter type against fine dust. The DeWalt HEPA handheld led, followed by the wet/dry DeWalt's washable HEPA-class element. Basic foam filters scored lowest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wet and dry capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which models are rated for liquids. Three of six are wet/dry, which matters on jobsites. Dry-only units were graded for dust work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared a 1/2-gallon, a 7.5 liter and a 2.5-gallon tank against carry weight. The compact units scored best for portability. Tank size decided the heavy-debris ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and cost of entry
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered whether a battery family is shared with other tools. Bare-tool listings lost points for buyers starting from zero. Existing owners gained.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read owner feedback patterns on filter clogging, latch durability and noise. Tool-platform vacuums earn praise for durability and criticism for bulk. Bare-tool listings were ranked with the cost of a battery in mind.

cards.label: Handheld
cards.text: The DeWalt HEPA and wet/dry units and the dustbusters hold one-handed, so they suit benches, cabs and ladders. They hold little.

cards.label: Compact tank
cards.text: The Milwaukee VC2-0 and FPOVCL carry more debris and are carried by handle. They are heavier and less nimble.

howToChoose.note: Pick a handheld for bench and vehicle work, and a compact tank unit for room cleanup.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a HEPA element, a washable filter and a canister release that does not puff dust back at you.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DeWalt 20V HEPA handheld is the pick, with the wet/dry DeWalt as the choice if the job also involves liquids.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the DeWalt HEPA handheld if you sand or cut every day. Cheaper filters clog and leak fine dust.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the Black+Decker models if the job is crumbs, not construction. A cheap dustbuster fits a front desk.

maintenance.why: A full tank loses airflow and adds weight. Empty wet debris the same day.
Fine dust clogs HEPA elements fast. Drywall dust packs the pleats within days, and airflow drops with it.
Damp parts breed mould in a closed tank. Dry fully with the lid off.
Hoses split at the flex point and seals pick up grit. Replace early to keep airflow.
Lithium packs fade when hot or empty. Keep them off vehicle dashboards.

faq.q: Is there a true industrial handheld vacuum?
faq.a: Not in the way there is an industrial drill. The closest options are tool-platform vacuums from DeWalt and Milwaukee, which are built for site use.

faq.q: Do I need a HEPA filter?
faq.a: If you make fine dust from drywall or concrete, yes. A foam filter lets the smallest particles pass through.
Only the wet/dry models can. The DeWalt hand vac and both Milwaukee units are wet/dry; the DeWalt HEPA handheld is dry only.
Many are bare tools. Check the listing for the words kit, battery or charger before buying.

faq.q: Should an office buy a jobsite vacuum?
faq.a: Usually not. A light dustbuster is quieter and quicker for crumbs, while a tool vac suits construction dust.
The motors outlast the batteries. Plan on a pack replacement after a few years, and replace filters when clogged.
